In probability theory, a '''log-t distribution''' or '''log-Student t distribution''' is a [[probability distribution]] of a [[random variable]] whose [[logarithm]] is distributed in accordance with a [[Student's t-distribution]]. If ''X'' is a random variable with a Student's t-distribution, then ''Y'' = [[exponential function|exp(''X'')]] has a log-t distribution; likewise, if ''Y'' has a log-t distribution, then ''X''&nbsp;=&nbsp;log(''Y'') has a Student's t-distribution.<ref name=logt>{{cite journal|journal=Revista Colombiana de Estadística - Applied Statistics|accessdate=2022-04-01|date=January 2022|volume=45|issue=1|pages=209–229|title=Some Inferential Problems from Log Student's T-distribution and its Multivariate Extension|author=Olosunde, Akinlolu & Olofintuade, Sylvester|doi=10.15446/rce.v45n1.90672|url=https://www.proquest.com/openview/70d41b2007ad2f9ade89ed9ef6eba775/1?pq-origsite=gscholar&cbl=2035762|doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Characterization==
The log-t distribution has the [[probability density function]]:
:<math>p(x\mid \nu,\hat{\mu},\hat{\sigma}) = \frac{\Gamma(\frac{\nu + 1}{2})}{x\Gamma(\frac{\nu}{2})\sqrt{\pi\nu}\hat\sigma\,} \left(1+\frac{1}{\nu}\left( \frac{ \ln x-\hat{\mu} } {\hat{\sigma} } \right)^2\right)^{-\frac{\nu+1}{2}} </math>,

where <math>\hat{\mu}</math> is the [[location parameter]] of the underlying (non-standardized) Student's t-distribution, <math>\hat{\sigma}</math> is the [[scale parameter]] of the underlying (non-standardized) Student's t-distribution, and <math>\nu</math> is the number of [[degrees of freedom]] of the underlying Student's t-distribution.<ref name=logt/>  If <math>\hat{\mu}=0</math> and <math>\hat{\sigma}=1</math> then the underlying distribution is the standardized Student's t-distribution.

If <math>\nu=1</math> then the distribution is a [[log-Cauchy distribution]].<ref name=logt/>  As <math>\nu</math> approaches [[infinity]], the distribution approaches a [[log-normal distribution]].<ref name=logt/><ref>{{cite book|title=Life Distributions: Structure of Nonparametric, Semiparametric, and Parametric Families|page=445|author1=Marshall, Albert W.|author2=Olkin, Ingram|year=2007|publisher=Springer|isbn=978-1921209680}}</ref>  Although the log-normal distribution has finite [[moment (mathematics)|moment]]s, for any finite degrees of freedom, the [[mean]] and [[variance]] and all higher [[moment (mathematics)|moment]]s of the log-t distribution are infinite or do not exist.<ref name=logt/>

The log-t distribution is a special case of the [[generalized beta distribution]] of the [[generalized_beta_distribution#Generalized beta of the second kind (GB2)|second kind]].<ref name=logt/><ref name=gb2>{{cite journal|title=A General Distribution for Describing Security Price Returns|author1=Bookstaber, Richard M.|author2=McDonald, James B.|journal=The Journal of Business|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2352878|accessdate=2022-04-05|date=July 1987|volume=60|issue=3|pages=401–424|publisher=University of Chicago Press|doi=10.1086/296404|jstor=2352878|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Some Generalized Mixture Distributions with an Application to Unemployment Duration|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1927230|doi=10.2307/1927230|author1=McDonald, James B.|author2=Butler, Richard J.|date=May 1987|pages=232–240|volume=69|issue=2|journal=The Review of Economics and Statistics|jstor=1927230|url-access=subscription}}</ref>  The log-t distribution is an example of a [[compound probability distribution]] between the lognormal distribution and [[inverse gamma distribution]] whereby the variance parameter of the lognormal distribution is a random variable distributed according to an inverse gamma distribution.<ref name=gb2/><ref>{{cite journal|title=Log-symmetric distributions: Statistical properties and parameter estimation|author1=Vanegas, Luis Hernando|author2=Paula, Gilberto A.|journal=Brazilian Journal of Probability and Statistics|doi=10.1214/14-BJPS272|year=2016|volume=30|issue=2|pages=196–220|doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Applications==
The log-t distribution has applications in finance.<ref name=gb2/>  For example, the distribution of stock market returns often shows fatter tails than a [[normal distribution]], and thus tends to fit a Student's t-distribution better than a normal distribution.  While the [[Black-Scholes model]] based on the log-normal distribution is often used to price [[stock options]], option pricing formulas based on the log-t distribution can be a preferable alternative if the returns have fat tails.<ref name=options>{{cite journal|title=Pricing European Options with a Log Student's t-Distribution: a Gosset Formula|author=Cassidy, Daniel T.|author2=Hamp, Michael J.|author3=Ouyed, Rachid|journal=Physica A |year=2010|volume= 389|issue= 24|pages= 5736–5748|doi=10.1016/j.physa.2010.08.037|arxiv=0906.4092 |bibcode=2010PhyA..389.5736C|s2cid=100313689}}</ref>  The fact that the log-t distribution has infinite mean is a problem when using it to value options, but there are techniques to overcome that limitation, such as by truncating the probability density function at some arbitrary large value.<ref name=options/><ref>{{cite journal|title=A Jump-Diffusion Model for Option Pricing|author=Kou, S.G.|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/822677|accessdate=2022-04-05|date=August 2022|journal=Management Science|volume=48|issue=8|pages=1086–1101|doi=10.1287/mnsc.48.8.1086.166|jstor=822677|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Option Pricing with Heavy-tailed Distributions of Logarithmic Returns|author1=Basnarkov, Lasko|author2=Stojkoski, Viktor|author3=Utkovski, Zoran|author4=Kocarev, Ljupco|year=2019|journal=International Journal of Theoretical and Applied Finance|volume=22|issue=7|doi=10.1142/S0219024919500419|arxiv=1807.01756|s2cid=121129552}}</ref>

The log-t distribution also has applications in [[hydrology]] and in analyzing data on [[cancer]] remission.<ref name=logt/><ref>{{cite journal|title=On the sampling distribution of the coefficient of L-variation for hydrological applications|author=Viglione, A.|url=https://www.hydrol-earth-syst-sci-discuss.net/7/5467/2010/hessd-7-5467-2010.pdf|accessdate=2022-04-01|year=2010|journal=Hydrology and Earth System Sciences Discussions|volume=7|pages=5467–5496|doi=10.5194/hessd-7-5467-2010 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

==Multivariate log-t distribution==
Analogous to the log-normal distribution, [[multivariate distribution|multivariate]] forms of the log-t distribution exist.  In this case, the location parameter is replaced by a vector '''''μ''''', the scale parameter is replaced by a matrix '''Σ'''.<ref name=logt/>
